5-6: A recipe scaled to a different number of people.
A total shared in a ratio, between two or three, or as a prize for the work each did: each share, or the gap between two.
Two kinds in a ratio, and the difference between them.
Two bags of beads, each in its own ratio, tipped into one box: the ratio in the box.
Gear wheels: the turns of one wheel against the turns of the other.
A mixture in a ratio, and the most that can be made from what there is.
Three kinds linked by two ratios: the share of each.
A ratio that changes when some are added: the amounts at the start.
A map scale: the real distance from the distance on the map.
Loaves eaten in equal shares by three, two of whom brought them: how the third one's coins are shared fairly.
Fish marked, let go and caught again: the share of marked fish in the new catch is taken as their share in the whole pond, which gives its size.
Two candles of different lengths, each burning down at its own steady rate in a known time, are equally long after a while: how their lengths compared at first.
Two kinds at two prices mixed to sell at a price between them: the ratio to mix them in, from how far each price is from the price of the mix.
Two juices, a can of each enough for so many cans of a drink made of both: when the mix changes and a can of drink holds the same, how many cans one juice is now enough for.
Two herds that mix two kinds of cows give the same milk in different numbers of days: which kind gives more, from what each kind gives over all those days.
Workers, work and days that change together, such as 7 wolves eating 7 sheep in 7 days: how the time changes when the workers and the work change by the same factor.
Half the way at one speed and half at another: the time over the whole way is not that at the average speed, so a rival at a steady speed can win.
A total that stays the same while the ratio of its shares changes, as money in a game of cards: the shares from what one of them gained or lost.
Two kinds in a group with their shares of the number and of the weight given in per cent: how many times heavier one kind is than the other on average.
Two eaters, one so many times faster at both dishes, swap dishes once and finish both together, sharing one dish equally: the part of the other dish each ate.
